headline: Superhuman acquires AI notetaker Fathom, valued at $94M with 400K active users
summary: Superhuman integrates Fathom's AI notetaking capabilities, leveraging its 400,000 monthly active users to enhance its productivity suite for agentic work.
details: Superhuman, a leading productivity platform, has acquired Y Combinator-backed AI notetaker Fathom. This move comes as productivity platforms increasingly aim to integrate advanced AI capabilities for automating work.

Fathom, founded in 2020, had raised over $30 million in funding and was valued at $94 million in 2024. Its investor list includes Zoom Apps Fund, Telescope Partners, and individuals like Reddit CEO Steve Huffman.

The acquisition allows Superhuman to quickly add a robust notetaking solution rather than building one internally. Superhuman's CEO, Shishir Mehrotra, noted the complexity of creating a high-quality notetaker after internal testing.
Fathom boasts a significant user base with over 400,000 monthly active users and more than 1 million recorded meetings to date. Its generous free plan contributed to this widespread adoption.

Superhuman plans to leverage Fathom's technology to proactively start work and surface meeting context in real time. This integration will enable AI agents to extract insights and automate tasks based on meeting data.

The meeting notetaker market is highly competitive, with startups like Granola and Read AI also raising substantial funding. Market pressure to offer more than just basic notetaking capabilities influenced Fathom's decision.

Fathom's CEO, Richard White, highlighted Superhuman's massive 40 million user base as a key opportunity for scaling. The acquisition provides Fathom with immediate distribution and access to a broader platform.

Fathom will integrate into Superhuman's existing suite, which includes an email client, docs app, calendar, database solution, and an AI agent builder platform. This will enable streamlined workflows, such as drafting emails, updating data, and scheduling follow-ups directly from meeting insights.

headline_marked: New $100K [[H-1B Visa Fee Pushes Tech Jobs Offshore]]
headline: New $100K H-1B Visa Fee Pushes Tech Jobs Offshore
summary: Shifting rules around H-1B visas have introduced a substantial new fee, prompting companies to build and hire elsewhere to mitigate costs.
details: New regulations are imposing a significant $100,000 fee for H-1B visas, drastically increasing the cost for tech companies seeking to employ foreign talent. This policy change is forcing businesses to re-evaluate their operational and hiring strategies.

As a direct result of these heightened costs, many tech companies are now actively exploring options to establish operations and hire personnel outside the United States. This strategic shift aims to circumvent the financial burden associated with the new visa fees.

The impact is particularly felt within the technology sector, which has historically relied on the H-1B program to fill specialized roles and address skill gaps. This trend suggests a potential decrease in domestic tech job growth and a corresponding increase in offshore development and employment.

Lucas Laursen, technology policy editor at IEEE Spectrum, highlights how these shifting rules are compelling companies to build and hire in other countries. The long-term effects on the US tech industry's competitiveness and talent pool remain a key concern.
